memoryText: I have set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
readingInstruction: Today there is no new reading. Yesterday you completed the Unit 2 review; today closes the week with rest. Take time to let both the doctrinal weight of Unit 2 and the rhythm of weekly Sabbath settle into your heart.
memoryVerseMeditation:
The rainbow is the sign of the Noahic Covenant, God’s promise never to destroy the earth by flood again. In the ancient Near East, a bow was a weapon. Here, God hangs his bow in the sky with the string pointing AWAY from the earth, as if to say: my weapon of judgment has been laid down.

Every rainbow you have ever seen is a reminder of this covenant, and a promise that God’s judgment is not the last word for his world. The covenant is universal in scope, made with “every living creature” on earth. Every harvest, every sunrise, every breath taken on this planet is a gift under this covenant.

Carry this verse with you this week. The next time you see a rainbow, say it. The next time it rains, remember the bow that hangs above the storm. By next week, the verse should be yours.
weekInReview:
The week centered on the Noahic Covenant. You read Genesis 8:20-9:29, Noah’s first sacrifice after the flood, God’s resolve never to curse the ground again, the institution of the rainbow as covenant sign. You read Genesis 10-11, the Table of Nations and the tower of Babel, humanity’s pride scattered into the diverse peoples that the gospel would one day gather. You worshiped through Psalm 36 (God’s steadfast love), Psalm 33:10-22 (God’s sovereignty over nations), and Psalm 9 (the justice of God who hears the cry of the oppressed). And yesterday you completed the Unit 2 review, with Genesis 6:8 as the anchor, Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD.

The week’s theme is the foundation of common grace. Every harvest, every birth in every culture, every flicker of beauty in a fallen world, all of it operates under the Noahic Covenant. God preserves the world he made, so that redemption can unfold within it.
reflectionQuestions: Where in your life have you been taking common grace for granted? The Noahic Covenant is the foundation of every meal you eat, every season you enjoy, every breath you draw. These are gifts, not entitlements. Name one specific gift of common grace today, and receive it as such.

How does the Noahic Covenant point you to Christ? God’s commitment to preserve the world after the flood was not the end of the story, it was the structural promise that held creation together so that the deeper covenant in Christ could come. The rainbow promises that God’s judgment is not final; the cross proves it. Where do you most need the assurance today that judgment is not the final word for those in Christ?

How does the tower of Babel reshape how you see today’s news? Humanity still gathers in pride. Humanity still tries to ascend to heaven on its own terms. Humanity still gets scattered. Where in your own life or your culture do you see Babel patterns? Where do you see Pentecost answers?
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the rainbow, the seasons, and every harvest, and name one you enjoyed this week.
Ask him to open your eyes to common grace in the days ahead.
Rest in the deeper grace that has reached you in his Son.
